extracted.intended_audience: investors, utility managers, regulators and analysts focused on electric utilities and nature/wildfire risk
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for identifying, assessing, disclosing and mitigating nature-related risks (especially wildfire risk) for electric transmission and distribution utilities. Covers dimensions of nature risk, materiality assessment, mitigation measures, disclosure frameworks and financial/governance responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature risk dimensions / manifestations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature-related risks manifest across multiple dimensions: Acute, Chronic, Legal and policy, Market, Technology, Reputational, Physical risk, Transition risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document uses these categories to characterise how nature risk affects a utility (e.g., wildfire events as acute/physical/legal risks leading to reputational and market impacts). Use this multi-dimensional framing when assessing threats to operations and value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify nature dependencies and impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand both how operations depend on natural systems (dependencies) and how operations affect those systems (impacts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first step is understanding nature dependencies and impacts, achievable through reporting and disclosure frameworks and by selecting relevant metrics and targets. Better identification, assessment and disclosure would increase awareness and likelihood of preventive actions being taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality assessment using ENCORE / sector materiality matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and prioritise impact drivers using materiality tools (e.g., Global Canopy / UNEP ENCORE materiality matrix) that identify sector-specific impacts on ecosystem services and natural capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ENCORE matrix identifies seven impact drivers of nature loss for the sector; use such a matrix to rate drivers as highly/very highly material to the business. Apply sector-specific materiality findings to focus mitigation and disclosure efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor key impact drivers (water use/pollution, GHGs, soil pollutants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track specific environmental impact drivers that are rated highly material for electric transmission and distribution operations, including water use and pollution, greenhouse gas emissions, and soil pollutants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report flags these drivers as rated highly or very highly material to nature loss for the sector; include them among selected metrics and targets for impact management and disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify nature dependency in economic terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the proportion of economic value generation that is dependent on nature (e.g., share of gross value added moderately or highly dependent on nature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dependency metrics to inform risk exposure and materiality (the report cites 100% of direct economic value generation for electric utilities as moderately or highly dependent). These figures support investor/stakeholder assessments of systemic exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure upgrades and monitoring systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in upgraded transmission and distribution equipment and monitoring systems to reduce the likelihood of operations igniting wildfires and to detect faults earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include replacing aging towers, installing upgraded lines, and deploying enhanced monitoring systems; the report cites PG&E’s required investments and pledges (e.g., billions committed) as part of post-liability remediation and risk reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vegetation management and equipment maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement rigorous vegetation management (tree trimming) and proactive maintenance/programs to ensure equipment is within its useful life and does not spark fires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report highlights legal findings that failures to trim trees and maintain equipment caused fires; ensure contractor oversight, documented trimming regimes, and timely replacement of aging infrastructure (e.g., towers past useful life).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational mitigations: public safety power shutoffs (PSPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use operational measures such as temporary suspension of electricity services under high wildfire-risk weather conditions to prevent ignition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSPS programs can mitigate ignition risk but cause customer outages and other impacts (the report notes thousands of customers can be left without power). Balance operational safety against social and economic impacts and document protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wildfire prediction and modelling (including AI tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt improved wildfire prediction and risk-modelling tools (including AI-based models) to anticipate outbreaks and inform preventative actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report names startups/solutions (Kettle, Zesty.AI, Cape Analytics) developing models used by insurers and utilities; integrate predictive analytics into planning, PSPS decision-making, and pre-season preparedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurance and financial risk management
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess insurance coverage adequacy and use modelling to inform re/insurance strategies; recognise that liabilities can exceed insurance limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PG&E’s liabilities exceeded insurance limits leading to bankruptcy; insurers/reinsurers are using new modelling services to price and manage exposure. Use models to engage with insurers, adjust coverage, and quantify residual financial risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal compliance and liability exposure assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify legal obligations and liability exposures from operations (e.g., duty to trim vegetation, maintain infrastructure), and assess litigation and regulatory risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal failures (e.g., pleading guilty to counts related to fatalities, large settlements) can lead to bankruptcy, criminal charges, and long-term reputational harm. Incorporate legal risk analysis into materiality and mitigation planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate governance, funding and remediation commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure governance structures and financing mechanisms are in place to fund mitigation/remediation (e.g., reorganisation, pledges for prevention, share offerings to shore up capital).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report describes PG&E’s court-ordered reorganisation, leadership change, and multi-billion dollar pledges for prevention; strong governance and credible funding commitments can restore investor/regulatory confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise safety in strategic planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Make safety (especially wildfire safety) a top strategic priority for utilities operating in high-risk regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report states ensuring safety should be a top priority; incorporate safety-driven capital allocation, operational KPIs, and stakeholder communication into long-term strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for climate–nature feedback loops
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise and incorporate interactions between climate change and nature loss (e.g., wildfires both result from and contribute to climate change), which can amplify future risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite evidence (Nature study) that anthropogenic warming increases wildfire growth frequency; integrate climate projections into wildfire risk scenarios and adaptation planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sector-specific tools and disclosure frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage sector tools (Global Canopy, UNEP ENCORE) and established reporting/disclosure frameworks to inform assessments and stakeholder reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report recommends use of these tools for information specific to electric power transmission and distribution and infrastructure holdings; couple tool outputs with chosen metrics/targets for disclosure to investors and regulators.
